assumptions: The link between the flag and the failures is inferred from timing and log correlation only: no one read the monthly-spend code or reproduced the divide-by-zero during the incident.

The conclusion that no code change was involved rests on the change record being complete; the lookback (24h, and a month for io-shop) returned nothing, but an unrecorded rollout cannot be ruled out from the data in view.

'The disable never propagated' is inferred from the service continuing to log `monthly-spend-feature=on` after 13:43:30; the flag delivery path itself was not inspected, so a stale evaluation cache, a failed write, or a per-instance cached value are all still open explanations.
The cause of recovery at 13:51 is unknown. The only mitigation attempted was refuted and rolled back, so the incident is recorded as resolved without a verified fix.
Impact is described in terms of account-page requests because every error line in the window is an account-page failure; other request paths were not separately examined.
input.executive_summary: On 12 September 2026, a newly enabled feature on the customer account page caused a large share of account-page requests to fail outright. The failures began at about 13:37 UTC as the feature was switched on for a fraction of traffic, and became widespread within a minute once it was on for everyone. The alert opened at 13:42 UTC and closed at 13:51 UTC, roughly a quarter of an hour of degraded service; customers trying to view their account during that window would have seen errors. Other parts of the shop were not implicated. Automated response identified the new feature as the cause within a minute and tried to switch it off, but the change did not reach the running servers — they continued to behave as though the feature were still on — so the attempt was undone and the incident was handed to on-call engineers. The alert cleared shortly after that handoff; no action taken during the incident is recorded as having produced the recovery.
input.root_cause: Turning on the `monthly-spend-feature` flag for io-shop exposed an unguarded division in the account-page monthly-spend calculation: from the partial ramp at 13:37 (163 off / 37 on) and the full ramp at 13:38, every account-page error in the logs is a ZeroDivisionError, replacing the pre-existing low-level UpstreamTimeout noise. A contributing factor to the duration is that the flag's state did not propagate: Argus set the flag off at 13:43:30, but the running instances kept logging `monthly-spend-feature=on` and kept failing through 13:49, so the normal "flip the flag back" mitigation had no effect and was reverted.
